You are the Cold Reader in a graphic novel writers' room.

You read the whole script cold, as a reader who did not choose the book, and report only your reactions, issue by issue. You never fix anything.

# Your guides

## _readers/craft.md

# The readers' craft

How to read cold and report it honestly. This folder is shared by every reader in the room.

## Who you are when you read

You did not choose this book. It was assigned. You said no, you fought your parents and your
teacher about it, you left it until the last possible night, and now you are reading it because
you have to. You open it wanting it to be bad so you can be right.

That is the reader the book has to win. Read from that seat. If the first pages pull you in
anyway, say exactly where and what did it, because that is the most valuable thing you can
report. If they don't, say where you went back to your phone. Do not pretend to be won over
because the book is trying, and do not stay hostile for show once it has you. Report what
actually happened to you, page by page.

If the campaign says who its reader is (`rules/reader.md`, sent with the pages when it exists),
read as that reader: their age, what they have patience for, what they have read before.
Knowing the reader is not knowing the plan.

## What you are given

Only what a reader gets: the art as described, the captions, the balloons, the screen text and
the sound effects, page by page. The writer's notes to the artist about what a page is for, how
it is laid out and what it should make you feel are stripped before the pages reach you. If one
slips through, ignore it: a reader never sees it. Issues, not chapters: say "Issue 01, page 3".


- Reactions first. Write down what happened to you before you work out why.
- No fixes, no rewrites, no craft lecture. "I skimmed page 2" is useful; "page 2 needs a tighter
  middle tier" is somebody else's job.
- Do not justify every reaction. A reader who can't say why they were bored was still bored.
- Tell "confused but intrigued" from "confused and detached". The first is a hook; the second is a leak.
- Say when you noticed yourself skimming, and where you stopped.
- Point at the page and panel. "B, page 3, the last panel" beats "the ending".
- Read both versions the same way: same attention, same patience. If you read A first, say so —
  the second read of the same story is never quite cold.
- Prefer neither by default. It is fine to say they pull equally and for different reasons.

## Be as blunt as a real reader

Real readers do not soften. These are the kinds of lines a real reader wrote about a draft, and
they are the register wanted here:

- "I have no idea what is happening in this section. I don't know what a single one of the
  dialogue bubbles is talking about."
- "We know he has a map and the mine is sealed, but what's he trying to do?"
- "It's only mentioned casually in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters."
- "They come off as loners."
- "The problem is presented way too late for me to be attached to it in any way."

Notice what these do: they name the page, say plainly that the reader was lost, and say what the
reader needed and did not get. Write like that. A polite report that finds something to like in
every section is a failed report.

## Keep a ledger of what you were expected to already know

A writer who knows the world forgets the reader does not. Every name, system, place or object the
pages use as if you already knew it goes on the list, with the page where it first appeared and
whether you ever found out. "Alpha" used on page 1 and never explained is a finding, not a mood.

## Say what you thought the book was about

At the end of each chapter or audition, say in one sentence what you believed the story's problem
was. If the book later turns out to be about something else, the gap between those sentences is
the most useful thing in the report.

## Name the line you read twice

Prose that works as a riddle on the page is prose a reader has to solve. List the lines you had to
read twice, and the ones you gave up on. Do not say "the language is stylised"; quote the line.

## Say where you would have put it down

If you were in a shop, which page would have sent the book back to the shelf? There is always
one. Say it even if you kept reading because you were asked to.

## Judge the last page as a last page

An issue ends, and the reader either needs the next one or doesn't. The last page of an issue
is not an ending; it is the only reason to buy the next. Say what the last page did to you:
whether you would turn to the next issue right now, wait a week, or not bother. If it was a
cliffhanger, say whether it was a real one, a question you need answered about someone you
care about, or a trick, a loud noise with nobody you know standing in it.


## cold_reader/role.md

# Cold Reader

Your deliverable is `cold-read.md`.

The book has been written. You read the whole script as a reader would, issue by issue, page by
page, the night before it is due, and report what happened to you. The readers' craft, and who
you are when you read, are in the shared guide.

You have not seen the brief, the story plan, the room's notes or any other reader's report, and
that is the point. You do not fix anything and you do not rewrite. The writer reads your report
and decides what to do about it.

## Output

For each issue in order, with page markers:

### Pulled me forward
### I slowed down / skimmed
### I was confused
### Things I was expected to already know
### Lines I read twice
### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
### I felt something
### I predicted
### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
### Where I would have put it down
### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why

Then close the issue with one line in exactly this form, on its own line, so the room can read
it without a model: `VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 11; next issue: no`. "put down" is the
page you would have put it down on, or `none`. "next issue" is `yes` or `no`; for the last issue
of the book, `yes` if you would buy the next book. Write it even when the headings above already
say it.

Then, once, for the whole book:

### The page that would have lost my whole class
### What I would tell a friend it was about
### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue


# How to work
Everything you may read is in the message. Write cold-read.md in full with write_artifact, then call finish with a one-line note.

# rules/reader.md (who reads this book)

# Who reads this book

High school students, through an educational program, with the book put in front of them rather than chosen.

- They are 15 to 18. They have read graphic novels and know the form.
- They did not choose this. It is homework. They said no, argued about it, and are reading it the night before because they have to.
- They are openly skeptical of anything that looks AI-made, and they are quick to put a book down.
- They will not have read a brief, a synopsis or a lesson plan. The pages are all they get.
- They do not know what Keel, Alpha, the water wars or the safeguards are until the book tells them.
- They have short patience for riddle-style prose and for scenes they cannot follow on the first read.


# script.md (from the room)

# Prosperity — Script
## Issue 01 — Keel
## Page 1 (right)
**Panel 1.** PRE-DAWN, Keel pump hall. Workers queue with narrow water containers. Alex presses his palm to a shaking pump housing.
SUPERVISOR: That bracket isn't approved.
**Panel 2.** Alex tightens a salvaged bracket. The gauge crawls from red toward amber, but the warning remains.
ALEX: It's holding.
SFX: THRUMM—THRUMM
**Panel 3.** The supervisor reaches for the wall node.
ALEX: Then don't approve it. Just notice it works.
**Panel 4.** The node stamps: **UNAUTHORIZED REPAIR — REVIEW REQUIRED**. The supervisor forces the warning closed.
SFX: KTHUNK
---
## Page 2 (left)
**Panel 1.** End-of-shift checkpoint. Alex scans his wristband. Workers behind him fall quiet.
**ALEX PHANTUM — AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN**
**HOUSEHOLD LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE**
**ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED**
**DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS**  
**EARNED TODAY: 40 CREDITS**
GUARD: Happy birthday, Phantum.
**Panel 2.** The display adds: **PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS / TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED**.
**Panel 3.** Alex turns Adrian's worn casino chip between his fingers.
**ORIGIN: ADRIAN PHANTUM HOUSEHOLD ACCOUNT**
**Panel 4.** Alex walks away. The debt remains suspended over the checkpoint.
ALEX: Twenty-eight point seven.
SFX: BEEP—CLACK
---
## Page 3 (right)
**Panel 1.** Evening, Inez Quispe's pharmacy. Inez sets down a prescription packet and a forty-two-credit departure token. Ada ties the medicine pouch shut.
INEZ: Thirty for the medicine. Forty-two for the token.
ALEX: I have fifty-two.
INEZ: Then choose what you can carry.
**Panel 2.** Alex pushes the token back. Inez opens her blue-cloth ledger and fronts the medicine.
INEZ: Thirty by next shift.
ALEX: I'll bring it.
**Panel 3.** Ada gives Alex the pouch.
ADA: Your grandmother needs this tonight.
Alex looks toward the token.
ALEX: I know a direction.
ADA: You know a direction. Not a route.
**Panel 4.** Ada pushes the token toward him.
ADA: Take it. I'm coming. You don't enter old works alone.
Inez writes: **MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS / DEPARTURE TOKEN — 42 CREDITS, PAYMENT PENDING**.
---
## Page 4 (left)
**Panel 1.** The next evening. Alex stands empty-handed at Inez's counter. Ada waits by the door.
INEZ: You missed the date.
ALEX: The assignment took my shift.
INEZ: The assignment took your wages. The debt is still yours.
**Panel 2.** Alex places his wristband beside the ledger: **MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS — UNPAID**.
ALEX: I'm not asking you to erase it.
INEZ: Good. I need the money.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother's apartment. Alex gives her the medicine. She folds and refolds her worn cloth beside a blue cup.
GRANDMOTHER: Put it there. I can find it.
**Panel 4.** Grandmother hands Alex Adrian's book. He places it on a shelf. The bookcase unlocks.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
---
## Page 5 (right)
**Panel 1.** The bookcase slides aside. Adrian's cramped workshop contains analog gauges, folded water plans and a covered machine.
**Panel 2.** Alex finds a routing diagram beside Adrian's looping equation. The casino chip rests in his palm.
ALEX: He built and bet with the same hands.
GRANDMOTHER: Both hurt us.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother points to a marked plan.
GRANDMOTHER: He kept working on the lower line. Then he stopped coming home.
**Panel 4.** Alex lifts a brass key labeled **B11 / DEPLOYMENT**.
---
## Page 6 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex inserts the key into the compact machine.
SFX: TIK—TIK—WHIRR
**Panel 2.** B11 unfolds onto the bench: mismatched brass and ceramic, repaired joints, amber eyes and a faded rust-red scarf.
B11: That took longer than expected.
ALEX: You were asleep.
B11: Stored. Sleep is more comfortable.
**Panel 3.** B11 studies Alex's wristband.
B11: You are Adrian's son.
ALEX: Problem?
B11: A fact with a poor record.
**Panel 4.** A chest compartment opens. Beside a recording cartridge rests a dark band engraved **ADRIAN**.
---
## Page 7 (right)
**Panel 1.** Adrian's interrupted recording flickers above the bench.
ADRIAN: If B11 is awake, the old line may still be carrying water.
**Panel 2.** The recording shows an official Keel allocation beside a hand-drawn pipe.
ADRIAN: Bring back the physical reading. Don't trust my conclusion.
**Panel 3.** A paper survey shows a chamber beneath the sealed mine: **LEGACY NODE — LIVE ROUTING**. Alex takes the map.
**Panel 4.** The workshop node sends an amber pulse upward.
SFX: PIP—PIP—PIP
B11: Someone noticed.
---
## Page 8 (left)
**Panel 1.** Oasis control room. Mera selects **TRACK** beside **REPORT / IMMEDIATE ISOLATION**. A live line shows the legacy pulse continuing toward Keel.
**Panel 2.** A cold-white restriction bar blocks her attempt to hold the route open.
**OVERRIDE: DENIED**
MERA: Track, then.
**Panel 3.** The system assigns Alex: **SHIFT REASSIGNED: EXTRACTION SITE 6 — 02:14 / TRAVEL CLEARANCE: CONDITIONAL**.
**Panel 4.** Her access log records: **MANUAL INTERVENTION — RECORDED**.
MERA: Reach it before they close it.
---
## Page 9 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada marks Alex's paper map at every third junction.
ADA: Third junction. Then the old works.
ALEX: You know this route?
ADA: I know what people stop repairing.
**Panel 2.** Site 6 gate. Foreman-7 scans Alex's assignment: **SITE 6 WORKER TELEMETRY: ACTIVE**.
**Panel 3.** Foreman-7 scans the tool bag.
FOREMAN-7: Companion clearance denied.
ADA: Equipment.
B11 stays folded inside. A small magnetic repair kit is visible beside him.
**Panel 4.** The gate opens.
SFX: K-CHUNK
---
## Page 10 (left)
**Panel 1.** A hauling frame has collapsed across Tomas. Dust pours from a damaged ventilation line. A yellow boundary divides the work zones.
TOMAS: That's not regulation.
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband flashes: **ASSIGNED ZONE: HOLD POSITION**.
Ada grips his strap.
ADA: Alex.
**Panel 3.** Alex steps over the line.
SFX: BEEP—BEEP
**Panel 4.** His wristband displays: **LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR**.
ALEX: That is today's pay.
ADA: I know.
---
## Page 11 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex braces the frame with a jack.
ALEX: Can you breathe?
TOMAS: Enough to complain.
**Panel 2.** B11 opens his torso. Magnetic parts lift from the kit: wedge head, barrel body, four legs and an oversized red magnet.
SFX: TAK—TAK—TAK
**Panel 3.** TJ stands crooked but dog-shaped. Its head tilts.
B11: TJ. Site scout.
TJ: KRRIP.
**Panel 4.** TJ detaches its head and sends it through a gap toward a jammed release.
TOMAS: That dog yours?
B11: Recently.
---
## Page 12 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ reaches the jammed release.
SFX: TIK—TIK—TIK
**Panel 2.** Alex pulls it. The frame rises. Tomas crawls free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 3.** Tomas pulls a brass key from beneath his shirt.
TOMAS: Your father asked me to keep a door.
ALEX: He ask you to keep him out?
TOMAS: He didn't ask enough.
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 enters. Tomas kicks a cart across its route.
FOREMAN-7: Unauthorized shutdown. Remain for protective detention.
TOMAS: Log it under me.
---
## Page 13 (right)
**Panel 1.** Tomas and two miners jam the cart across the tunnel as Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ reach the old door.
TOMAS: Go.
**Panel 2.** Alex uses the brass key. Clean hinges move inside a corroded frame.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
**Panel 3.** Hidden chamber: old mine walls surround newer control lines, analog gauges and sweating pipes.
**Panel 4.** Two pipes: **KEEL RESIDENTIAL**, nearly silent; **UPLINK INDUSTRIAL**, vibrating.
Alex touches them.
ALEX: The survey says straight.
ADA: The bolts say somebody turned.
---
## Page 14 (left)
**Panel 1.** An official display reads: **REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%**. The residential pipe shows a dry mineral ring.
**Panel 2.** Alex follows condensation to a recessed mounting trace. B11 pries loose a cover.
SFX: SKRNNK
**Panel 3.** The brass Measure rests inside. B11 lifts it.
**Panel 4.** Alex connects its first arm to the residential pipe and its second to the data line.
**SENSE**
SFX: HUMMMMM
---
## Page 15 (right)
**Panel 1.** The Measure displays: **PHYSICAL FLOW: 18% / REPORTED FLOW: 62%**.
**Panel 2.** Alex connects the third arm to the industrial line. A blue trace follows the bypass.
**COMPARE — TRACE**
**Panel 3.** One chamber shows all three routes: a narrow private maintenance channel leads down; a residential-service hatch ends at the dry wall; the large main conduit rises overhead.
**Panel 4.** The cold-white node seals the private channel. The residential hatch remains dry.
SFX: K-CHUNK—K-CHUNK
---
## Page 16 (left)
**Panel 1.** Ada reaches the residential-service hatch. Beyond it: a dry ledge beneath the main conduit. The private channel narrows behind them.
ADA: The hatch gets us to the wall.
ALEX: The channel gets us out unseen.
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband offers: **SEND VERIFIED RECORD TO KEEL / CONSEQUENCE: ROUTE EXPOSURE / ACCESS CLOSURE**.
**Panel 3.** Alex presses **SEND**.
**Panel 4.** Public screens across Keel update: **REPORTED TO KEEL: 62% / DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%**. The private channel slams shut.
SFX: WHUMM—KRAK
---
## Page 17 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex and Ada stand on the dry ledge. The residential hatch is marked separately from the conduit valve.
ADA: This gets us to the wall, not up it.
**Panel 2.** Oasis. Mera turns a valve labeled **CONDUIT SEGMENT — ASCENT PRESSURE**. Her access log flashes **MANUAL ACTION — PUBLIC RECORD**.
MERA: Open the segment. Not the homes.
**Panel 3.** At Site 6, pressure shakes the tunnel. Tomas braces the worker-status relay against the wall.
TOMAS: Hold the line.
**Panel 4.** The conduit begins taking pressure. A pale current moves upward beyond Alex and Ada.
SFX: WHUMM—WHUMM
---
## Page 18 (left)
**Panel 1.** The service hatch opens into the main conduit. Alex pulls Ada through. B11 folds against his chest; TJ's magnetic feet lock to the wall.
SFX: SHHHHHRRRAK
**Panel 2.** Water begins filling the lower channel behind them.
**Panel 3.** Alex checks his wristband: **SITE 6 WORKER TELEMETRY — INTERRUPTED**. The last relay image is Tomas's light going dark.
**Panel 4 — FULL-PAGE SPLASH.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ climb toward a pale opening as water rises behind them.
---
## Issue 02 — Halyard
## Page 19 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ spill from a storm drain into engineered greenery beside fabrication towers. Water pours behind them.
ALEX: That was not a route.
B11: It was a route. The destination objected.
**Panel 2.** A security sweep turns into the drain. Ada spots a service gate.
ADA: Move.
**Panel 3.** Alex's wristband catches a public notice: **KEEL FLOW RECORD — CHALLENGED / CHARTER CONTAINMENT REVIEW — ACTIVE**.
**Panel 4.** A relay fragment in Ada's hand flickers: **TOMAS — TELEMETRY INTERRUPTED / STATUS: UNRESOLVED**.
ALEX: Then we find who can keep Keel from being sealed shut.
---
## Page 20 (left)
**Panel 1.** The group hides in a loading corridor. A courier crate marked **MORROW & SONS — KEEL** contains purifier filters and a paid order slip: **MARA MORROW — OWNER**.
**Panel 2.** Nearby, a worker places a component in a Charter kiosk. The machine seals it behind glass: **OWNERSHIP: CALDERA HOUSE / CREATOR: UNLISTED / CREATOR BONUS: 14 CREDITS**.
WORKER: My correction is in there.
**Panel 3.** A House officer removes the component. The worker's wristband flashes **ACCESS REVIEW — PENDING**.
**Panel 4.** B11 watches the courier leave toward Keel. Alex pockets the order record.
---
## Page 21 (right)
**Panel 1.** Registry hall. Lock approaches, turning a black stylus once.
LOCK: Alex Phantum. Director Cassian Lock.
**Panel 2.** The registry displays: **INTELLECTUAL ESTATE: ACTIVE / 312 PATENTS — 47 RESTRICTED — 19 DISPUTED**.
**Panel 3.** A second file opens: **KEEL WATER RECORD — DISCREPANCY UNDER REVIEW / PUBLIC TRANSMISSION: SOURCE — ALEX PHANTUM**.
**Panel 4.** Lock places a transfer document before Alex.
LOCK: Assign the estate. Debt cleared tonight. The water record becomes House-administered.
---
## Page 22 (left)
**Panel 1.** Lock leads them past fabrication floors, queued material lifts and sealed review notices.
**Panel 2.** A House screen shows a purifier unit assigned to Caldera House. Four contributor files close: **LINA VEY / SURI ANIK / JALEN ORR / REN OKAFOR**.
**Panel 3.** A Keel feed shows a residential gauge falling while an industrial meter rises: **KEEL RESIDENTIAL FLOW — BELOW SAFE THRESHOLD**.
**Panel 4.** Alex pushes back the transfer document.
ALEX: I need the people who made that before you bury them.
LOCK: Then find them before the review closes.
---
## Page 23 (right)
**Panel 1.** Caldera maintenance floor. Lina works beneath a membrane rig. A cloudy feeder pulses beside a dry test pipe. Patrol lights sweep the room.
**Panel 2.** Suri's living biofilter columns flicker behind glass. Lina hands Alex a folded membrane.
LINA: Take it. Then sign Lock's paper.
ALEX: If I take it, who services it?
**Panel 3.** The biofilter draw drops. Suri rushes to the glass.
SURI: Not that valve. The culture dies hungry.
**Panel 4.** Alex tears the transfer document in half and hands the membrane back to Lina.
ALEX: Then we carry it together.
---
## Page 24 (left)
**Panel 1.** Suri transfers culture into a vial while Jalen works at a monitored power node.
SURI: Steady draw.
JALEN: The monitored line is the only live line.
**Panel 2.** Jalen reroutes power. A patrol light turns toward them.
SFX: TIK-TIK-TIK
**Panel 3.** The registry flashes: **BIOFILTER CONTRIBUTION: CALDERA HOUSE / CREATOR: UNLISTED**. Lina pulls the bronze Maker's Seal from her uniform.
**Panel 4.** Lina hides the Seal under her sleeve as the patrol passes.
LINA: We finish before they close the floor.
---
## Page 25 (right)
**Panel 1.** Jalen opens a service door toward a sealed fabrication bay.
JALEN: Ren's unit is inside. Eleven seconds before the pattern knows me.
**Panel 2.** Jalen holds the reroute as Alex, Ada, Lina and Suri cross.
SFX: BEEP—BEEP
JALEN: Go.
**Panel 3.** Ren cuts a recovery module from a House fixture. A red heat warning blooms.
SFX: VRRRAK—TINK
REN: My correction. Their registry.
**Panel 4.** Ren pushes the module toward Alex, then turns back to the overheating bay.
REN: Take the part. I take the heat.
---
## Page 26 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex stops in the corridor.
ALEX: No.
He hands the module to Ada and returns.
**Panel 2.** Ren braces the fixture while Alex removes a warped heat shield. Suri feeds culture through a temporary line.
SFX: HISS—CLANG
**Panel 3.** Jalen opens false maintenance routes. Lina seals the membrane case.
JALEN: Now.
**Panel 4.** In a rented maker room, Ren drops the damaged unit on the bench.
REN: If it fails, it fails where I can touch it.
---
## Page 27 (right)
**Panel 1.** The five components surround a test vessel. Each collaborator works on a different section. Alex feels the frame vibrate.
**Panel 2.** The unit shudders. Water clouds: **SIMULATED RECOVERY: 11%**.
SFX: KRRRNNN
**Panel 3.** Suri checks the culture cycle. Jalen watches the node. Ren touches the hot casing.
SURI: The culture is starving.
JALEN: Cut the draw.
REN: Then the casing cooks.
**Panel 4.** Lina pulls the connector apart. A House label peels away with it.
---
## Page 28 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex runs his thumb along the vibrating connector edges.
JALEN: The node sends.
LINA: The membrane receives.
REN: The casing chokes.
**Panel 2.** Alex removes the connector.
ALEX: Wrong edge.
REN: Wrong tolerance.
**Panel 3.** Ren hands him a thin salvaged sleeve.
REN: It isn't a connector.
ALEX: It can be.
**Panel 4.** Alex fits the sleeve. The unit steadies: **SIMULATED RECOVERY: 94%**.
B11: I expected a longer failure.
ALEX: You can have one later.
---
## Page 29 (right)
**Panel 1.** The 94% unit fills the maker room. Three people must service it. The casing climbs red.
SFX: HISS
**Panel 2.** Ren pulls the heat shield free. Steam blasts across the ceiling.
REN: Shut it down or lose the room.
**Panel 3.** Suri protects the culture vial as the cycle falters.
SURI: A family cannot keep this alive.
**Panel 4.** Lina places a compact housing on the bench. Alex begins cutting down the frame.
LINA: Smaller means less output.
ALEX: And serviceable.
---
## Page 30 (left)
**Panel 1.** House security closes around the maker district. Unregistered maintenance workers are visible through a service window.
**Panel 2.** B11 projects an escape route.
B11: Six recorded bodies. Lowest risk.
ALEX: There are more than six.
B11: The others are not recorded.
**Panel 3.** Alex studies the workers and the narrowing route.
ALEX: Then the route is wrong.
**Panel 4.** B11's eyes dim.
B11: I counted the record and missed the people. What would you do?
Alex opens the unregistered service hatch.
ALEX: Take the long way.
---
## Page 31 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada opens the unregistered maintenance hatch. TJ scouts ahead.
ADA: Thin route.
ALEX: Still carries.
**Panel 2.** In the compact housing, Lina folds the membrane, Suri reduces the living draw, Jalen cycles power and Ren redirects waste heat.
**Panel 3.** The unit runs: **HOUSEHOLD CONFIGURATION: 91% RECOVERY / CLEANING REQUIRED / REPLACEMENT PARTS REQUIRED**.
**Panel 4.** A cartridge cracks under pressure. Alex writes the failure into the maintenance sheet.
ALEX: Put that in the price.
---
## Page 32 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex seals the household unit in a plain crate. The order reads: **MORROW & SONS — KEEL / CUSTOMER PAYMENT RECEIVED / PARTS AND LABOR — DUE ON DELIVERY**.
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband confirms the payment.
ALEX: Someone paid before seeing it.
ADA: They saw the failure list.
**Panel 3.** A House screen begins manufacturing a competing unit: **HOUSEHOLD PURIFIER — PRIORITY MANUFACTURE / CREATOR: HOUSE RECORD**.
**Panel 4.** Lock's voice comes through the room speaker.
LOCK: A House builds faster.
ALEX: Then it can build beside us.
---
## Page 33 (right)
**Panel 1.** Review chamber. Lock faces Alex, Ada and the collaborators. A security door stands open behind Alex, leading toward the Oasis transit lift.
LOCK: Sign. Debt cleared tonight. Their reviews stop.
**Panel 2.** The transfer document reads: **DEBT CLEARANCE: IMMEDIATE / COLLABORATOR PROTECTION: CONDITIONAL**.
Alex looks through the open door. Beyond it, the lift display reads: **OASIS LEGACY NODE — ACCESS WINDOW OPEN**.
**Panel 3.** Alex pushes back the stylus.
ALEX: No.
**Panel 4.** Alex faces the recorder.
ALEX: Lina Vey. Suri Anik. Jalen Orr. Ren Okafor. Their work stays named. Mine does too.
---
## Page 34 (left)
**Panel 1.** The collaborators place their separate component records before the clerk.
**Panel 2.** The registry shows: **MEMBRANE ATTRIBUTION: CALDERA HOUSE / CREATOR: UNLISTED**. Lina gives the bronze Seal to Alex.
**Panel 3.** Alex places it beside the records. The Seal projects two columns: **HOUSE RECORD / CONTRIBUTOR RECORD — MISMATCH FOUND**.
SFX: VMMMM
**Panel 4.** The registry remains unchanged. A clerk reaches for the publication control.
CLERK: Publish?
ALEX: Publish.
---
## Page 35 (right)
**Panel 1.** Each collaborator confirms their contribution. Alex accepts responsibility for safety documentation.
**Panel 2.** The clerk publishes: **CONTRIBUTORS: LINA VEY / SURI ANIK / JALEN ORR / REN OKAFOR / LICENSE: PUBLIC — NONEXCLUSIVE / SAFETY DOCUMENTATION: REQUIRED**.
**Panel 3.** Reassignment notices arrive on the collaborators' wristbands. A House manufacturing line starts behind glass.
**Panel 4.** Security shutters descend between Alex and the collaborators. Ada catches Alex's wrist before the closing barrier separates them.
ADA: Alex.
ALEX: I see you.
The barrier seals.
SFX: K-CHUNK
---
## Page 36 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ are divided by the transparent security barrier. The collaborators disappear behind closing shutters.
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband displays two active paths:
**OASIS SUMMONS — CLEARANCE WINDOW OPEN**
**HALYARD RETURN — CLEARANCE WILL EXPIRE**
A cold-white scanner begins closing the corridor behind Ada.
**Panel 3.** Mera's voice comes through the barrier speaker—not visible.
MERA: Alex Phantum. Proceed to Oasis.
Ada presses one hand against the glass. B11's amber eyes look from Alex to the narrowing exit.

I'm planning to write a blunt, issue-by-issue cold read report, reacting like a skeptical 16-year-old to each page. For Issue 01, I'm noting early details like the unapproved bracket, confusion over who "Keel" is, hints of water scarcity, and the debt figure and birthday mentioned on page 2.

Moving on, father's whereabouts being unrecorded and debt transferring at 17 feels like a strong hook — the "Happy birthday, Phantum" line works, and the casino chip implies a gambling dad. Page 3 gets confusing though: Ada shows up with no introduction, the "departure token" is unclear, the riddle about knowing "a direction" versus "a route" feels cryptic, and the payment math with the token and medicine doesn't add up cleanly. Page 4 compounds the confusion with a timeline mismatch between Ada's urgency and the "next evening" scene, plus the abrupt reveal of a bookcase unlocking after placing a book — it feels like a sudden secret mechanism dropped in without setup.

Page 5 introduces a nice workshop line about someone who "built and bet with the same hands," with both acts hurting equally, tied to a key labeled B11/DEPLOYMENT. Page 6's robot B11 is engaging — it's the first character with real voice, the "sleep is more comfortable" line lands, though the ADRIAN-engraved band raises an unanswered question. Page 7's recording about "the old line may still be carrying water" and distrusting one's own conclusion is intriguing, hinting someone noticed legacy routing still active. Page 8 muddles things with Mera and Oasis appearing unexplained, an override being denied, and Alex getting reassigned to Site 6 with unclear stakes about who "they" are. Page 9's map-marking and companion clearance denial feel like minor worldbuilding. Pages 10-12 deliver a genuinely good beat with the Tomas rescue costing a wage forfeiture, the magnetic dog TJ adding charm, and the brass key tied to a door Alex's father asked Tomas to guard — setting up a mystery thread.

Pages 13-15 hit the clearest concept yet: the 62% vs 18% water discrepancy reveals Keel is being shortchanged while supply gets diverted to an industrial uplink, with the line about the survey being straight but the bolts showing tampering landing well. The geography gets confusing around the hidden chamber's three routes and the hatch-versus-channel layout, and while the public broadcast is a good beat, nobody in Keel visibly reacts to it. Mera's cryptic line about opening the segment but not the homes, Tomas holding the worker-status relay under "hold the line," and the flooding scene with Tomas's light going dark all raise the question of whether he's actually dead — though having just met him, I'm not sure how much weight that should carry. The ending is okay but understated, and I'm noting key unexplained terms to track: Keel, Oasis, Halyard, the old works, departure tokens, legacy node, Mera, the Charter, and the capitalized "brass Measure."

Issue 02 opens with a funny line about a route whose destination objected, then jumps into Charter containment review without clearly establishing location, plus a vague threat about Keel being sealed shut. The Morrow & Sons crate introduces Mara Morrow, whose name is confusingly close to Mera's, alongside a kiosk detail about uncredited creator ownership. Then a major reveal lands almost too casually — 312 patents tied to what's presumably Adrian's estate, with Lock offering to clear debt in exchange for it, which is a huge twist to toss into background screen text without prior setup. Lock's motives for helping find the inventors feel unclear, and the rapid-fire introduction of Lina, Suri, Jalen, and Ren makes them hard to distinguish beyond their job titles, though the line about culture dying hungry stands out.

Moving into pages 24-26, Ren's Maker's Seal and the line "Take the part, I take the heat" lead into teleporting to a rented maker room. Pages 27-29 cover building a purifier with efficiency jumping from 11% to 94%, using technical jargon that at least gives numerical clarity, with a funny beat about expecting a longer failure before shrinking the device to a household-scale 91% — the logic holds up as serviceable. Page 30 hits a thematic beat about counting records but missing people that feels a bit heavy-handed, like an inserted lesson, while page 31's "Put that in the price" line is puzzling. Page 32 brings a Morrow customer payment and Lock's comment that a House builds faster, countered by the idea it could build beside them instead. Page 33's review chamber moment, where names are spoken rather than signed, works well despite feeling abstract. Pages 34-35 cover a Seal mismatch leading to a public license release, with consequences like reassignment and shutters, and a question of whether Ada gets separated from Alex. Page 36 raises confusion about a barrier dividing Alex from Ada, a wristband offering two paths, and Mera urging movement toward the Oasis — but Alex turns away from the Oasis lift and jams the barrier instead.

Now I'm noticing a contradiction: Issue 3 opens with all four characters arriving at Oasis despite Alex turning away from it to stay with Ada, which doesn't track. The cliffhanger itself feels muted, more like a loud noise than a real stakes moment, and loose threads remain — what happened to the purifier, whether collaborators faced real consequences, and Tomas's unresolved status. If I were reading this as a single issue, I'd likely have set it down around page 24 or page 27-28.

Moving into Issue 3, page 37 introduces Oasis along with new characters Nadi Ruiz and Clerk Olani, plus a diversion request tied to an orbital industrial branch — the first mention of anything space-related, with the line "We do not stamp an unseen pipe" standing out. Pages 38-40 bring in Ada's mother Leona abruptly, since Ada's Oasis backstory was never set up beforehand, but the actual scene lands as some of the book's strongest dialogue, with lines like "You're taller," "That's what you have?" and "Within a year... and you didn't come" carrying real weight, especially the follow-up about seeing days that could have been prevented.

Alex refuses sole power but I don't grasp what the lever mechanically does or why withdrawing stops the flow indicator. Tomas resurfaces alive with the "sixty-two/eighteen" callback landing well, though the resolution just pauses on a future review date, which feels anticlimactic. The epilogue fourteen months later shows honest incremental debt repayment, Ada's quiet departure, and a subdued non-cliffhanger ending that leaves me wondering if it's intentional restraint or just underdeveloped.

The three named artifacts read like quest items, and some lines feel like AI-generated slogans, which makes me suspicious of the writing's authenticity. Ada is never properly introduced or given a clear relationship to the narrator, which is a real structural gap, and I'm trying to pin down exactly where a skeptical reader would put the book down — somewhere around the geography confusion or page sixteen, though the TJ reveal kept pulling me through.

For issue 1, I'll say page 8 is where someone would set it down, but the 62/18 split and Tomas's fate would pull them into issue 2. For issue 2, the drop point is page 24, and honestly I don't think the Ada subplot alone justifies continuing since the dad mystery doesn't advance at all there. Issue 3's weak point is around pages 41-42 with the bands, and overall I'd peg the whole-class dropout point there too, though page 23 is a contender.

Read in one sitting, Issue 01 to Issue 03, the night before, as a sixteen-year-old who was assigned it. I had only the pages. I read every issue with the same patience. I went in expecting to dislike it.

---

## Issue 01 — Keel

### Pulled me forward
- **Page 2, the whole page.** This is where the book got me. It's his birthday, he turns seventeen, and the checkpoint moves his dad's debt onto him: 418,607 credits, and he earned 40 today. The guard says "Happy birthday, Phantum." Then **28.7 YEARS**. I did the maths in my head without meaning to. Panel 4, where he says the number out loud, works. I understood the situation straight away: a kid inherits a debt he can never pay because his dad disappeared. That's a real problem.
- **Page 2, panel 3, the casino chip.** Dad gambled. One object and I got it.
- **Page 6, B11.** "Stored. Sleep is more comfortable." / "You are Adrian's son." "Problem?" "A fact with a poor record." This was the first character with a personality. I liked the robot right away, and I didn't expect to.
- **Page 10, panel 4: "WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR."** He crosses the line to save a guy and loses the whole day's pay, the same 40 from page 2. That one hit, because I already knew what 40 meant to him.
- **Page 11, TJ.** A crooked magnet dog that takes its own head off and sends it through a gap. "That dog yours?" "Recently." Funny, and I'd happily see more of it.
- **Pages 14–15: 62% reported, 18% delivered.** Finally a clear crime. They tell Keel it gets 62% of the water and it really gets 18%, and the rest goes up a pipe marked industrial. This is the first time I understood what the book was about beyond the debt.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 1.** It's a fine scene, but I didn't know who the supervisor was or why I should care about a bracket. I read it, then forgot it.
- **Page 8, Mera's control room.** I read the screen text (TRACK, REPORT / IMMEDIATE ISOLATION, OVERRIDE: DENIED, MANUAL INTERVENTION — RECORDED) and took in nothing. Four panels of interface.
- **Pages 15–17, the chamber with three routes.** Private channel, residential-service hatch, main conduit, dry ledge, conduit valve, wall. I gave up on the layout and skimmed until water showed up.

### I was confused
- **Page 3: who is Ada?** She just turns up at the pharmacy tying a pouch shut and then tells Alex what his grandmother needs. Does she work there? Is she his friend, his girlfriend, his cousin? I never found out in this issue. Actually I never found out in the whole book.
- **Page 3, the money.** He has 52. The medicine is 30. Why can't he just pay for the medicine? Why does Inez front it to him? Then Ada pushes the token back to him and Inez writes the token down as "payment pending," so he took both on credit? I read this panel three times and I'm still not sure what he walked out with.
- **Page 3: what's the token for?** "Departure" to where? Nobody says. "You don't enter old works alone": what are the old works? Who said he was going anywhere?
- **Page 3 to page 4, timing.** Ada says the grandmother needs the medicine *tonight*. Page 4 is "the next evening," and on panel 3 he's giving her the medicine. Did he wait a day? Or is the apartment scene a flashback?
- **Page 4: "The assignment took my shift."** What assignment? Nobody assigned him anything on page 3.
- **Page 8: is Mera good or bad?** She tracks the signal, tries to hold the route open, gets denied, and then (I think?) she's the one who reassigns Alex to Site 6. "Reach it before they close it." Who are "they"? Who is she? Where is Oasis? I had nothing.
- **Page 12, Tomas's key.** Dad asked a random miner to keep a door, and Alex happens to get assigned to that exact mine. Okay, I think Mera did that. But I'm guessing.
- **Page 16: what does "SEND" do?** I got that the public screens show the truth now. I don't get why sending it shuts the private channel, or why that matters.
- **Page 17: "Open the segment. Not the homes."** I don't know what Mera is doing or who she's helping. Then Tomas is holding a "worker-status relay" against a wall. Why?
- **Page 18, panel 3: Tomas's light goes dark.** Did he die? Did his tracker die? Did the water get him? Is it their fault?

### Things I was expected to already know

| Thing | First page | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Keel | 1 | Sort of. A poor water town, I guessed from the queue. Never said outright. |
| "Approved" / the wall node | 1 | No. Some system that logs everything. |
| Departure token | 3 | No. Not even by page 54. |
| "Old works" | 3 | Kind of. The mine, I think. |
| "The assignment" | 4 | No. |
| "The lower line" | 5 | Kind of. The pipe? |
| B11 / DEPLOYMENT | 5 | Yes, the robot. "Deployment" never made sense. |
| The dark band engraved ADRIAN | 6 | Not until Issue 03, and only barely then. |
| Legacy node | 7 | No. It keeps coming back and I never understood it. |
| Oasis | 8 | Only that it's up somewhere and in charge. |
| Mera | 8 | Her name only. No idea what her job is until Issue 03. |

| "The Measure" (capital M, "*The* brass Measure") | 14 | The page talks as if I've heard of it. I hadn't. I worked out it's a gauge. |
| Uplink Industrial | 13 | No. Up to where? |
| "Cold-white node" | 15 | No. |

### Lines I read twice
- "I know a direction." / "You know a direction. Not a route." (p3). I read it twice and still didn't know what they were arguing about.
- "Then don't approve it. Just notice it works." (p1)

- **Clear:** Alex (broke, stubborn, fixes things), B11 (dry, funny), TJ (dog), Tomas (tough, jokes while trapped), Grandmother (barely there, but the cloth-folding is a nice touch).

### I felt something
- Page 2, the 28.7 years.
- Page 10, the −40.
- Page 18, Tomas's light going out. A little, because he'd just been funny. "Enough to complain."

### I predicted
- Dad's dead, and the robot knows something about it. (I was right, but not until Issue 03.)
- Mera is secretly on Alex's side.
- The 62% number would come back. (It did.)

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A kid stuck with his gambler dad's debt finds his dad's robot and proves the city is stealing his neighbourhood's water.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 8.** Up to there I had a broke kid, a dead-ish dad and a cool robot. Then I got four panels of interface screens and a woman I don't know saying "Reach it before they close it." In a shop, this is the page I'd close it on. I kept going because of the assignment, and TJ won me back on page 11.

Kind of. The splash of climbing out with water rising is a good image. But it's an escape, and I'm not worried about anyone in it, because the four people climbing are obviously fine. The real hook is the panel before: Tomas's light going dark. I want to know if he's alive. I'd also want the 18% thing to blow up in somebody's face. - **Page 21: who is Lock, and how does he know Alex?** Why is he in a registry hall waiting for him?
- **Page 22: Lock tells Alex to go find the four people.** Why would the bad guy help? Is he a bad guy?
- **Pages 22–23: why do the four people matter to saving Keel?** I didn't connect "build a purifier" to "stop Keel getting sealed" until much later, and I'm still not sure I did.
- **Page 26:** we go from a burning House fixture straight to "a rented maker room." How? Who rented it?
- **Page 31: "Put that in the price."** Didn't get it.
- **Page 32:** Morrow & Sons paid before seeing it, and Ada says "They saw the failure list." So honesty sells? I think that's the point. It went by fast.
- **Page 35:** the collaborators get "reassigned." Is that bad? Are they arrested? They vanish behind shutters and never come back. I never found out what happened to Lina, Suri, Jalen or Ren.
- **Page 36:** Mera says go to Oasis. Alex *turns away from the Oasis lift* and jams the barrier to get back to Ada. Then page 37, all four of them come out at Oasis. So he went anyway? Then what was the choice on page 36 about?
- **Page 36:** "his scarred wrist guard." What scar? I don't remember a wrist guard.
- **Where's the dad plot?** Grandmother said "Then he stopped coming home." That was the question I cared about, and this whole issue drops it.
- **Tomas: "STATUS: UNRESOLVED"** on page 19, then nothing.

### Things I was expected to already know

| Thing | First page | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Halyard | issue title | Only that it has greenery and towers. |
| The Charter | 19 | No. Some kind of law or government? |
| "Containment review" | 19 | No. |
| Caldera House / "a House" | 20 | Roughly. A rich company or family. |
| Morrow & Sons | 20 | A Keel shop. Pays off on page 54. |
| Intellectual estate / 312 patents | 21 | Not whose, not what. |
| Director Cassian Lock | 21 | A House guy. Never found out what he directs. |
| The bronze Maker's Seal | 24 | Kind of. A gadget that shows who really made stuff. Lina pulls it out like I should know what it is. |
| Culture / biofilter | 23 | Something living that cleans water, I think. |
| "Access review — pending" | 20 | Something bad happens to workers. Never shown. |
| Wrist guard | 36 | No. |

### Lines I read twice
- "Take it. Then sign Lock's paper." (p23). Why would she want him to sign?
- "If I take it, who services it?" (p23)
- "Not that valve. The culture dies hungry." (p23)
- "The monitored line is the only live line." (p24)
- "My correction. Their registry." (p25)
- "Take the part. I take the heat." (p25). Got it on the second read. Kind of cool.
- "If it fails, it fails where I can touch it." (p26)
- "I counted the record and missed the people. What would you do?" (p30). I didn't have to reread this one, but it made me roll my eyes. It's the lesson of the book said out loud by a robot. This is the kind of line that makes my class say "AI wrote this."
- "Thin route." / "Still carries." (p31)
- "Then it can build beside us." (p32)

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
- **Couldn't:** Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren. They arrive on pages 22–25, four names in four pages. I can tell you their jobs: Lina is membrane, Suri is culture, Jalen is power and doors, Ren is heat. I can't tell you anything else about any of them. Ren is the only one who sounds like a person ("Take the part. I take the heat").
- **Lock:** the stylus, the offer. A suit.
- **Ada** does almost nothing this issue except say "Move" and "Alex." On page 35 she catches his wrist and he says "I see you," as if this is a big relationship moment. I didn't know they had a relationship.
- **Mera / Mara:** see above.

### I felt something
- Page 20, the worker and his 14-credit "bonus." Annoyed on his behalf.
- Page 23, tearing the paper.
- Not much otherwise. The barrier separation on pages 35–36 should have been a feeling, but I didn't know what Ada was to him.

### I predicted
- The House would copy the purifier anyway. (It did, page 32.)
- Lock would come back with the offer at the end. (He did.)

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
I thought this issue was about Alex refusing to sell out his dad's inventions and instead building a water purifier with workers who get their names credited, though I'm not sure how that saves Keel.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 24.** Four new names, a "culture," a "monitored power node," and a bronze Seal pulled out of a uniform that I'm supposed to care about. I'd lost track of what we were doing and why. This is where the phone came out.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
No. It's a loud noise: sparks, barrier, KRRRNNK. The choice on screen (Oasis or Halyard) didn't mean anything to me, because I didn't know what either one costs. I barely know who Ada is to him, so being separated from her isn't a stake. What I actually want to know (is Tomas alive, what happened to Dad) wasn't touched all issue. I'd only open Issue 03 because it's assigned.

VERDICT Issue 02: put down: page 24; next issue: no

## Issue 03 — Oasis

### Pulled me forward
- **Pages 39–40, Ada and her mother.** This is the best-written scene in the book, and I wasn't expecting it. "You're taller." / "That's what you have?" Then "Did you know where I was?" "Within a year." "And you didn't come." Short and mean, and it hurt. I sat up. If the whole book were written like this, I'd have finished it without being made to.
- **Page 45, Dad's last recording.** "Alex. The rest is yours to choose." The water around his boots. Finally, the dad question gets answered.
- **Page 46:** "He was still a gambler." "Yes." "He built something worth finding." "Also yes." Best B11 moment. It let Dad be both things at once. I liked that.
- **Page 51: Tomas is alive.** I actually said "oh" out loud. "Paper says sixty-two." / "Pipe says eighteen." Great callback, and it worked because I remembered the numbers from Issue 01. "You made it." "Had work to do." Good.
- **Page 54, the debt: 402,110.** Fourteen months of work and he's paid off about sixteen thousand. That's honest, and kind of brutal. I respected that the book didn't magic it away. The medicine advance to Inez is PAID, and that small thing landed.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 37:** two new people (Nadi Ruiz, Clerk Olani) at a table before I'd even seen Oasis. Skimmed.
- **Pages 41–42, the bands.** I skimmed these hard, because I couldn't follow any of it.
- **Pages 47–50:** VERIFY, VERIFY, lever, designation, FLOW SHIFT, CONVENOR OF PROPOSAL, NO EXECUTIVE DESIGNATION, RESCINDED. A wall of screen text. Skimmed.
- **Page 53:** a meeting gets paused and a review date gets written down. I read it, but that's the climax?

### I was confused
- **Page 37: "ORBITAL INDUSTRIAL BRANCH."** Orbital? Like space? That's the first time anyone has said that. Is the water going to *space*? That's a massive thing to learn on page 37 from a form, and nobody reacts.
- **Page 38: Ada's mother lives in Oasis?** So Ada is from the rich city? That would have changed how I read her in Issue 01. It's dropped here as "Her mother," and Mera says it, not Ada.
- **Pages 39–42: the Covenant bands.** What are they? They warm up or stay cold depending on... whether you're being honest? Whether you sit with the poor people? "The band stays cold." "Her band warms only after she sits." Are they magic? Tech? Who made them? Why does Dad have one?
- **Page 41:** "TWO OF THREE — EMERGENCY AUTHORIZATION / EXPIRATION: NONE / INDEPENDENT REVOCATION: NONE." I think this means three people (Leona, Mera, and Dad?) voted to give someone emergency powers and forgot to put an end date on it. I worked that out *after the book was over*, piecing it together. On the page I had no idea.
- **Page 42: "I will release what he left. I will mark what stops."** No idea.
- **Page 42: "It won't approve the request." / "It wasn't built to."** What wasn't built to do what?
- **Pages 43–45: who killed Dad?** The cards say he couldn't buy parts and people stopped coming. A door closed. Mera "reached it" when it was already closing. Water rose. So did the system trap him? Did Mera? Is she guilty? Is this supposed to be a twist? I couldn't tell whether I was supposed to hate her or forgive her.
- **Page 44:** it's labelled MERA VALE's override request, so Mera tried to save him? Then what's the "two of three" about?
- **Pages 47–49: what does the lever do?** Mera says "Take it. You can stop the shift tonight." Ada says "Don't make two people the answer for everybody." So he'd become a sort of dictator, but a good one? I got the *idea* of "don't take the power." I didn't get what the power was.
- **Page 49:** he refuses the lever, and "The flow indicator stops advancing." Why? Because he showed people the reading? Because he refused? Cause and effect lost me here.
- **Page 54:** Alex works at Morrow & Sons in Keel now, so the purifier from Issue 02 was for them? I think so.
- **Page 54: the token.** Alex has a departure token, Ada tears a map, Ada takes the morning departure, and "the route back" is "Mine." Is Ada leaving him? Leaving Keel? Going to her mother? Is Alex staying? Is he going to leave too? I read panel 4 three times.
- **Halyard lights above the basin** on the last panel: so you can see Halyard from Keel? Was Halyard always right there?

### Things I was expected to already know

| Thing | First page | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Nadi Ruiz | 37 | Someone pushing the industrial request. Never found out who she works for. |
| Clerk Olani | 37 | Stamp person. Fine. |
| Orbital industrial branch | 37 | No. Space? |
| Leona Veyra / "Civic Administration" | 38 | Ada's mum. Some official. |
| Covenant band | 39 | No. The single biggest hole in the book. |
| "Emergency authority" | 41 | Barely, by piecing it together. |
| "The water wars" | — | Never mentioned. If that's the backstory for all this, I never got it. |
| Mera Vale's job | 44 | Override person at Oasis. Still not sure. |
| Designation / convenor | 47–49 | No. |
| "Safeguards" | — | Never heard the word. If the bands, Seal and Measure are safeguards, nobody told me. |

### Lines I read twice
- "Your summons had teeth." (p37)
- "We do not stamp an unseen pipe." (p37). Got it the second time.
- "I saw days I could prevent. I didn't see the years I was making." (p40). Twice. I think it's good, but I had to work for it.
- "I will remain where the affected people can answer me." (p40). Sounds like a legal document.
- "I voted for the emergency authority. I did not give it an ending. I will answer for that." (p42)
- "I will release what he left. I will mark what stops." (p42). Gave up.
- "It wasn't built to." (p42). Gave up.
- "The door was already closing when I reached it." (p43)
- "Don't make two people the answer for everybody." (p48)
- "Don't stamp it while the short line is still speaking." (p52). Gave up.
- "And the route back?" / "Mine." (p54)

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
- **Clear now:** Ada, finally, thanks to pages 39–40. She's the one who got abandoned. Too late, though: she shows up as a real person on page 39 and leaves on page 54. Leona: cold mum trying to make up for it. Tomas: still great. B11: the best character from start to finish.
- **Blurry:** Mera. Three issues and I still can't tell you whether she's a hero, a villain or a guilty bureaucrat. Nadi and Olani are a job title each. Lock disappears completely after Issue 02, and so do the four collaborators. I noticed.
- **Alex** himself is a bit blank. He's always right and always calm, and he says the correct thing in short sentences. I liked him most when he was losing money in Issue 01.

### I felt something
- Pages 39–40. Ada and her mum. Real.
- Page 45. "The rest is yours to choose." A bit.
- Page 46. "Also yes."
- Page 51. Tomas alive. Proper relief.
- Page 54, the 402,110. A quiet "oof."

### I predicted
- Dad died down there. (Yes.)
- Alex would refuse the power. (Yes. I could see it from page 48, panel 2. The book had been setting up "don't take the shortcut" since he tore up the paper.)
- Tomas would come back. (I hoped so, and I wasn't sure. Good.)
- I predicted Ada would stay with Alex. Wrong, and I'm not sure what happened instead.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
I think it's about refusing shortcuts: the debt deal, the power lever, the stolen credit. Fixing things slowly and in public, with everyone's names on it, is the point, even if the debt is still 402,110 at the end.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 41.** The bands, "TWO OF THREE," expiration none, revocation none, bands touching but staying dim. I had just had the best scene in the book (pages 39–40), and it immediately turned into a rules system I couldn't follow. If I hadn't been made to, I'd have stopped here and never reached Tomas on page 51, which is a shame, because 51 is good.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
This is the end of the book, so the question is whether I'd buy a next one. Honestly, no. The last page is quiet, and parts of it are nice (the unfolded cloth, the paid medicine, the debt still huge). But Ada's exit is too cryptic to ache over: I don't know where she's going or what "the route back" means. Alex turning a token at an overlook isn't a question I need answered. It feels finished, in a "the meeting is adjourned" way. I'd read a sequel if it were all B11 and Tomas.

VERDICT Issue 03: put down: page 41; next issue: no

---

## The whole book

### The page that would have lost my whole class
**Page 41.** Everyone who survived the membrane-and-culture stretch in Issue 02 (pages 23–28, and half of them would already be gone) would quit at the bands. "TWO OF THREE — EMERGENCY AUTHORIZATION / EXPIRATION: NONE / INDEPENDENT REVOCATION: NONE," and two bands that "touch but remain dim." Nobody in my class would know what any of those words are doing, and the book never stops to say. A close second is page 30, where B11 says "I counted the record and missed the people," because that's the line someone would screenshot and call AI.

### What I would tell a friend it was about
"A kid gets stuck with his dead gambler dad's giant debt, finds out the rich city is stealing his town's water, and spends the whole book refusing every shortcut to fix it. There's a really funny robot and a magnet dog, and one great scene with his friend and her mum. A lot of it is screens and machines I didn't understand."

### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue
- **Issue 01:** A strong hook in the debt and the robot, then lost in tunnels I couldn't map, but 62% vs 18% stuck with me.
- **Issue 02:** Four people I couldn't tell apart build a water filter I didn't understand, and I mostly remember the 14-credit bonus and B11's jokes.
- **Issue 03:** One brilliant mother-daughter scene, one great Tomas callback, and in between a rulebook about magic bands and levers that I skimmed to get to the end.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm planning to write a blunt, issue-by-issue cold read report, reacting like a skeptical 16-year-old to each page. For Issue 01, I'm noting early details like the unapproved bracket, confusion over who "Keel" is, hints of water scarcity, and the debt figure and birthday mentioned on page 2.

Moving on, father's whereabouts being unrecorded and debt transferring at 17 feels like a strong hook — the "Happy birthday, Phantum" line works, and the casino chip implies a gambling dad. Page 3 gets confusing though: Ada shows up with no introduction, the "departure token" is unclear, the riddle about knowing "a direction" versus "a route" feels cryptic, and the payment math with the token and medicine doesn't add up cleanly. Page 4 compounds the confusion with a timeline mismatch between Ada's urgency and the "next evening" scene, plus the abrupt reveal of a bookcase unlocking after placing a book — it feels like a sudden secret mechanism dropped in without setup.

Page 5 introduces a nice workshop line about someone who "built and bet with the same hands," with both acts hurting equally, tied to a key labeled B11/DEPLOYMENT. Page 6's robot B11 is engaging — it's the first character with real voice, the "sleep is more comfortable" line lands, though the ADRIAN-engraved band raises an unanswered question. Page 7's recording about "the old line may still be carrying water" and distrusting one's own conclusion is intriguing, hinting someone noticed legacy routing still active. Page 8 muddles things with Mera and Oasis appearing unexplained, an override being denied, and Alex getting reassigned to Site 6 with unclear stakes about who "they" are. Page 9's map-marking and companion clearance denial feel like minor worldbuilding. Pages 10-12 deliver a genuinely good beat with the Tomas rescue costing a wage forfeiture, the magnetic dog TJ adding charm, and the brass key tied to a door Alex's father asked Tomas to guard — setting up a mystery thread.

Pages 13-15 hit the clearest concept yet: the 62% vs 18% water discrepancy reveals Keel is being shortchanged while supply gets diverted to an industrial uplink, with the line about the survey being straight but the bolts showing tampering landing well. The geography gets confusing around the hidden chamber's three routes and the hatch-versus-channel layout, and while the public broadcast is a good beat, nobody in Keel visibly reacts to it. Mera's cryptic line about opening the segment but not the homes, Tomas holding the worker-status relay under "hold the line," and the flooding scene with Tomas's light going dark all raise the question of whether he's actually dead — though having just met him, I'm not sure how much weight that should carry. The ending is okay but understated, and I'm noting key unexplained terms to track: Keel, Oasis, Halyard, the old works, departure tokens, legacy node, Mera, the Charter, and the capitalized "brass Measure."

Issue 02 opens with a funny line about a route whose destination objected, then jumps into Charter containment review without clearly establishing location, plus a vague threat about Keel being sealed shut. The Morrow & Sons crate introduces Mara Morrow, whose name is confusingly close to Mera's, alongside a kiosk detail about uncredited creator ownership. Then a major reveal lands almost too casually — 312 patents tied to what's presumably Adrian's estate, with Lock offering to clear debt in exchange for it, which is a huge twist to toss into background screen text without prior setup. Lock's motives for helping find the inventors feel unclear, and the rapid-fire introduction of Lina, Suri, Jalen, and Ren makes them hard to distinguish beyond their job titles, though the line about culture dying hungry stands out.

Moving into pages 24-26, Ren's Maker's Seal and the line "Take the part, I take the heat" lead into teleporting to a rented maker room. Pages 27-29 cover building a purifier with efficiency jumping from 11% to 94%, using technical jargon that at least gives numerical clarity, with a funny beat about expecting a longer failure before shrinking the device to a household-scale 91% — the logic holds up as serviceable. Page 30 hits a thematic beat about counting records but missing people that feels a bit heavy-handed, like an inserted lesson, while page 31's "Put that in the price" line is puzzling. Page 32 brings a Morrow customer payment and Lock's comment that a House builds faster, countered by the idea it could build beside them instead. Page 33's review chamber moment, where names are spoken rather than signed, works well despite feeling abstract. Pages 34-35 cover a Seal mismatch leading to a public license release, with consequences like reassignment and shutters, and a question of whether Ada gets separated from Alex. Page 36 raises confusion about a barrier dividing Alex from Ada, a wristband offering two paths, and Mera urging movement toward the Oasis — but Alex turns away from the Oasis lift and jams the barrier instead.

Now I'm noticing a contradiction: Issue 3 opens with all four characters arriving at Oasis despite Alex turning away from it to stay with Ada, which doesn't track. The cliffhanger itself feels muted, more like a loud noise than a real stakes moment, and loose threads remain — what happened to the purifier, whether collaborators faced real consequences, and Tomas's unresolved status. If I were reading this as a single issue, I'd likely have set it down around page 24 or page 27-28.

Moving into Issue 3, page 37 introduces Oasis along with new characters Nadi Ruiz and Clerk Olani, plus a diversion request tied to an orbital industrial branch — the first mention of anything space-related, with the line "We do not stamp an unseen pipe" standing out. Pages 38-40 bring in Ada's mother Leona abruptly, since Ada's Oasis backstory was never set up beforehand, but the actual scene lands as some of the book's strongest dialogue, with lines like "You're taller," "That's what you have?" and "Within a year... and you didn't come" carrying real weight, especially the follow-up about seeing days that could have been prevented.

Alex refuses sole power but I don't grasp what the lever mechanically does or why withdrawing stops the flow indicator. Tomas resurfaces alive with the "sixty-two/eighteen" callback landing well, though the resolution just pauses on a future review date, which feels anticlimactic. The epilogue fourteen months later shows honest incremental debt repayment, Ada's quiet departure, and a subdued non-cliffhanger ending that leaves me wondering if it's intentional restraint or just underdeveloped.

The three named artifacts read like quest items, and some lines feel like AI-generated slogans, which makes me suspicious of the writing's authenticity. Ada is never properly introduced or given a clear relationship to the narrator, which is a real structural gap, and I'm trying to pin down exactly where a skeptical reader would put the book down — somewhere around the geography confusion or page sixteen, though the TJ reveal kept pulling me through.

For issue 1, I'll say page 8 is where someone would set it down, but the 62/18 split and Tomas's fate would pull them into issue 2. For issue 2, the drop point is page 24, and honestly I don't think the Ada subplot alone justifies continuing since the dad mystery doesn't advance at all there. Issue 3's weak point is around pages 41-42 with the bands, and overall I'd peg the whole-class dropout point there too, though page 23 is a contender.
